points.quote: Page mode and edgeless mode are two views of the same Yjs doc, which is one block tree. ... Switching mode only changes how that tree is rendered.
Its children are one `affine:surface` block and the `affine:note` blocks.
The `affine:surface` block has one prop, `elements`. ... These are "surface elements" and are not blocks. They include shape, brush (freehand drawing), connector, text, mindmap and group
Notes hold the page-mode content (paragraphs, lists and so on). In edgeless mode they appear as movable cards.
Several block types are allowed as children of the surface block (`surface-model.ts`): `affine:frame`, `affine:image`, ... Notes sit beside the surface, not under it.
the `xywh` prop holds a serialized string like `"[x,y,w,h]"`. Block models expose it through `gfx-block-model.ts`, and elements use the same field.
`index` is a fractional-index string such as `'a0'`. The string's lexical order is the z-order. ... Blocks and elements share one index space, so they can be layered against each other.
A `group` element has a `children` Y.Map of `childId → true` ... A `frame` is a block. It keeps `childElementIds: Record<id, boolean>` and its own `xywh` and `index`
